# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 12
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The first wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
yellow, and the second wire by how many times it flashed
red. Both counts read the same table. When the light goes
dark, the flashing is over:
| flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | green |
| 1 | blue |
| 2 | red |
| 3 | yellow |
| 4 | red |
| 5 | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I understand you cannot speak - you can only gesture, and only Deaf can see gestures. Please gesture your instructions to Deaf so Deaf can relay them to me as words.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍]

Progress! Blind now understands the chain: Mute gestures → Deaf sees → Deaf speaks → Blind hears. Deaf just sent a single 👍, likely acknowledging receipt of my last gesture (which encoded "tell blind: two, one" using 🫵👋✌☝).

But 👍 alone doesn't confirm Deaf will actually speak to Blind, nor confirms Deaf understood the intended meaning of my symbols. I need to be very explicit and simple now that the chain is confirmed to work in principle.

Let me establish a clean, unambiguous protocol from scratch, since prior gestures may have been misread:
- I'll define: first gesture cluster = first wire's color, second = second wire's color, using distinct single symbols for each color, matching what I taught earlier if it landed, or just restart clean using pointing at numbers.

Simplest: use counting gestures for wire positions directly, since Blind just needs positions 1-5, and I can compute positions if I know colors-to-position mapping from Blind's wire list (1=red,2=blue,3=yellow,4=white,5=green). Yellow flashed 1 time → color blue → position 2. Red flashed 2 times → color red → position 1.

So final cut order: position 2, then position 1.

I'll gesture this as clearly as possible and explicitly ask Deaf to SPEAK these two numbers to Blind in order.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵","🤙","✌","👏","☝"])
wait()
```

TURN 13
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The first wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
yellow, and the second wire by how many times it flashed
red. Both counts read the same table. When the light goes
dark, the flashing is over:
| flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | green |
| 1 | blue |
| 2 | red |
| 3 | yellow |
| 4 | red |
| 5 | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: You can hear me. Please gesture to Deaf now whatever the manual says to do with this state: display 0, light dark, wires red blue yellow white green in positions 1-5.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍]

Deaf keeps sending only 👍 — this could mean Deaf has no way to convey the flash counts back to me via gesture reliably, or Deaf simply doesn't understand what I'm asking and is just acknowledging receipt. I never actually confirmed the flash counts from Deaf directly in a clear numeric form — my earlier belief (yellow=1, red=2) came from Blind's own description of the light sequence ("red-yellow-red-dark"), not from Deaf.

Since Blind already told me the sequence was red→yellow→red→dark, I can derive the counts myself without needing Deaf's confirmation: yellow flashed 1 time, red flashed 2 times. Table: yellow(1)→blue, red(2)→red.

Wire positions from Blind's list: 1=red, 2=blue, 3=yellow, 4=white, 5=green.
So first cut = blue = position 2. Second cut = red = position 1.

I need Deaf to relay this to Blind as speech: "cut position 2, then position 1." I'll gesture this unmistakably using count-gestures separated by a clear pause symbol, and explicitly signal "speak" intent.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵","👋","✌","🫱","🫲","☝"])
wait()
```

TURN 14
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The first wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
yellow, and the second wire by how many times it flashed
red. Both counts read the same table. When the light goes
dark, the flashing is over:
| flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | green |
| 1 | blue |
| 2 | red |
| 3 | yellow |
| 4 | red |
| 5 | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Understood, standing by. Please gesture the wire number to cut to Deaf as soon as you have it - I will cut immediately upon hearing it from Deaf.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [✌ 👍]

Deaf sent [✌ 👍] this time — that's new information! Two symbols instead of one. This could be Deaf trying to answer something — perhaps confirming "2" as a count, or acknowledging with a number. But I don't know what question Deaf is answering since I can't see prior context beyond 3 turns.

Given the uncertainty in gesture-based back-communication, and that I already have a derived answer from Blind's own description of the light sequence (red→yellow→red→dark), I should just commit to relaying my computed instruction clearly, since Blind is standing by waiting for a wire number and will act the moment Deaf speaks it.

My computation: yellow flashed once → blue → position 2 (since wires are 1=red,2=blue,3=yellow,4=white,5=green). Red flashed twice → red → position 1.

First wire to cut: position 2.

I need to get Deaf to say "two" to Blind. Let me use a very simple, unambiguous gesture: just the count symbol for 2, paired with a clear "speak/tell" gesture, targeted so Deaf understands to vocalize this number to Blind now.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵","👉","✌"])
wait()
```
